sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Every multi-row column grew a little wider on each click of a column's sort glyph — reported on a release page, where `release-tracks` declares 18 collapsable columns and the whole table crept sideways. `initCollapsableColumns()` measured the first `<li>` of each multi-row cell as `li.scrollWidth` with `white-space: nowrap`, and applied `that + 28` as `th.style.minWidth`. An `<li>` is a block box and MusicBrainz's own `<ul>`s carry `padding: 0`, so it fills its `<td>`'s content box exactly — and for a block box with no horizontal overflow `scrollWidth` returns `clientWidth`, i.e. the column's CURRENT rendered width rather than the item's own. A sort re-render reuses the existing `<thead>` untouched, so each click read back the width the previous click had forced, added 28 px and committed it: measured at +12 px per click per column on the reported page. The measurement is now `width: max-content`, which sizes to the content and is independent of the containing block — the same cure `_measureHeaderMinWidth()` already applies to the column drag floor.

A collapsable column's minimum width could never come back down. The value was only ever raised, and nothing cleared it, so a column stayed as wide as the widest first item it had ever rendered even after a filter removed that row. This feature's own floor is now stamped on the `<th>` as `data-mb-collapse-min-px` and released by the pass that recomputes it, so a fresh measurement replaces it. An auto-resize floor written to the same property is deliberately left alone — it is measured across the whole cell rather than its first item, is legitimately the larger of the two, and continues to win.
